Pocspetri 1 Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pócspetri, Hungary

Not demolished. One of two Jewish cemeteries recorded on Pócspetri's cadastral maps, appearing by 1871, with tombstones through 1944. Jewish settlement began in the early 19th century, growing from 45 residents in 1840 to a peak of 93 by 1880 before declining to 61 by 1944. The community joined the Orthodox stream after 1869's Schism in Hungarian Jewry; in 1944, its rabbi was Áron Teitelbaum (from Nyírbátor), and community leader/shochet Ignác Weinberger oversaw local affairs before deportation via the Nyíregyháza Ghetto to Auschwitz. The community was never revived after the war.
